means: One way into a tool: the interactive door for people, the structured door for agents and scripts.
An interaction written down - keys pressed, screens expected - run on every change, its screens kept as evidence.
not: A recording only: a scene also checks.

means: Where the whole is weakest right now, read from every project's data, to choose the next piece of work.
An idea a project rests on, with why it matters.
not: What a word means: that is the vocabulary.

means: A shared process that carries work from one state to the next - built, tested, delivered - which projects call, not copy.
Chosen by the observatory's keepers to stand in its navigation. Any lens can still be found without it.
An owned fork of someone else's code (Rhizoid's rhizcut): pinned to an exact upstream point, changed only as named patches each written to go home.
A choice taken, with why, and with what was rejected.
Minutes weighted by how draining they were (load 0-10, Borg CR10): five counts as one. A short heavy chore can outweigh a long light one.
A project's whole chain on one page: why it exists, what it must reach, how each step is delivered and proven, what is happening now.
A small daily job in each project that writes down what its work produced: commits, releases, test runs.
The observatory's reading of every marked project's tables, every few hours.
One of the three stretches of a path: working (it does its job), perfection (as good as it should be), ongoing perfection (it stays so).
Why a project exists, written by the project itself for someone who knows nothing about it.
not: A feature list, or a summary for insiders.

means: A grand view of a family of projects, declared as one small file in its own repository, found and drawn like any other.
How draining an action was this time, from 0 (nothing) through 5 (hard) to 10 (maximal), after Borg's CR10 scale of perceived exertion.
not: How long it took: that is minutes.

means: An action done by hand that a tool could do: counted with its minutes and load, and when it was done, until something automates it.
not: Bad work: it is a measure of where a tool would help, not a judgment.

means: The small file (oco.toml) by which a repository says: I am part of the commons, and here are my tables.
A step on a path, reached only when its evidence exists.
The mirror: it reads what projects say about themselves and draws it. No project needs it to work.
The commons' language and machinery: the tables, the mark, the gatherers and the checks - the blood and heart every project lives by.
What a project must reach: its milestones on three horizons, each with the evidence that proves it.
A repository with a mark. It keeps its own idea, path, workings and work, in its own data.
The look around before acting: the question asked, what was found in plain words, and the sources it rests on.
Done by hand often enough (three times) or heavily enough (30 effort-minutes) that it asks for a tool.
not: Bad, or forbidden: a saturated action is simply the next candidate for automation.

means: A work someone made that a project stands on - a book, a paper, a page - with what is taken from it.
not: Research: a source is what was read, research is the reading and what came of it.

means: The words a project speaks and exactly what they mean - and what they do not mean. ocoeco defines the shared words; a project adds its own.
not: Jargon: a vocabulary translates words into plain language.

means: What actually happens: the backlog, the log, and what the gatherers record.
How a project's steps are delivered and proven - its tools, checks, gatherers, tests and practices - each tied to the step it serves, with why we care. As in the workings of a clock.
not: A task to do: that is the backlog.
